title: CMA's - Triplex, Addition, Nightly Rental
summary: Craig analyzes complex property scenarios including a triplex/fourplex in Hurricane, UT, a home with unpermitted addition in West Jordan, and nightly rental considerations. Covers cross-collateralization issues with lenders, ADU regulations, unpermitted square footage valuation, short-term rental income analysis, and how to properly comp properties with unique characteristics.

broker_guidance.scenario: Client wants to buy a duplex/fourplex as single transaction
broker_guidance.guidance: Lender will NOT cross-collateralize properties in residential space. Must get two loans, two refis, two full sets of disclosures. Exception: portfolio lenders who hold loans in-house (not Fannie/Freddie). DSCR lenders may allow it - must check with them specifically.
broker_guidance.client_language: A standard lender won't do one loan across multiple properties. We'll need separate financing for each unit, or find a portfolio lender who holds loans in-house.

broker_guidance.guidance: Unpermitted square footage should NOT be valued at same rate as permitted. Typical approach: value permitted SF at market rate, unpermitted at 50% or less. Must disclose unpermitted status. Buyer should verify with city what would be required to permit it. Some buyers won't touch unpermitted.
broker_guidance.client_language: The unpermitted square footage is valued at a discount - typically 50% or less of the permitted space value. We need to verify with the city what it would take to permit it, and you'll need to disclose this when you sell.

broker_guidance.guidance: Don't trust seller's Airbnb numbers. Get actual Airbnb dashboard screenshots or tax returns. Look for seasonal variations. Calculate net, not gross. Factor in management costs, cleaning, utilities, platform fees. Compare to long-term rental rates as backup.
broker_guidance.client_language: We need actual Airbnb income documentation, not just what the seller tells us. I'll want to see dashboard screenshots or tax returns to verify the numbers.

broker_guidance.scenario: Comping a unique property (triplex, ADU, etc.)
broker_guidance.guidance: For unique properties, expand search radius and time frame. Look for similar use cases, not just similar structures. May need to comp as single-family plus ADU value, or find other multi-family in area. Document why comps were selected. Be transparent about limitations.
broker_guidance.client_language: This is a unique property, so we're expanding our search to find the most comparable sales. We may need to value it as a primary home plus separate ADU income.

broker_guidance.guidance: ADU rules vary dramatically by city. Some allow short-term rentals in ADUs, some don't. Parking requirements differ. Some cities require owner-occupancy. Always verify current zoning and ADU ordinance before marketing rental income potential.
broker_guidance.client_language: ADU regulations vary by city. We need to verify that this property can legally operate as an ADU and whether short-term rentals are permitted before we factor that income into the valuation.

steps: Identify property type and unique characteristics
Verify financing structure (single loan vs multiple loans)
Check for unpermitted additions and verify with city
For short-term rentals: verify actual income documentation
Expand comp search radius and time frame for unique properties
Value unpermitted space at discount (typically 50% or less)
Calculate both best-case and conservative income scenarios
Disclose all known issues and limitations
